question: In Table 1D-2, how is 'Road Work' abbreviated on a portable changeable message sign, and what may follow it?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Table 1D-2 shows that "Road Work" is abbreviated as "RD WK" for temporary messages on portable changeable message signs. The abbreviation has a prompt word that must follow it — either "Ahead" or a [Distance] — as shown in the example "RD WK 1 MILE." Because the table lists a prompt word for this entry, the abbreviation should not be displayed without the appropriate prompt word following it. Standards (mandatory): - "When the word messages shown in Table 1D-2 need to be abbreviated on a portable changeable message sign, the abbreviations shown in Table 1D-2 shall be used. Unless indicated by an asterisk, these abbreviations shall only be used on portable changeable message signs." Guidance (recommended): - The abbreviations for words listed in Table 1D-2 that also show a prompt word should not be used on a portable changeable message sign unless the prompt word shown in Table 1D-2 either precedes or follows the abbreviation, as applicable — for "Road Work" (RD WK), the prompt words "Ahead" or "[Distance]" follow the abbreviation. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 1D-2 (Sheet 1 of 2) shows the row for "Road Work" with the standard abbreviation "RD WK," a prompt word following the abbreviation of "Ahead, [Distance]," and the example "RD WK 1 MILE." [Image 2] repeats the same Table 1D-2 (Sheet 1 of 2) content confirming the "Road Work / RD WK / Ahead, [Distance] / RD WK 1 MILE" row. Citations: - Table 1D-2 (p.36) - Section 1D.08 Standard §2 (p.34) - Section 1D.08 Guidance §3 (p.34)
gold_answer: RD WK; it may be followed by AHEAD or a distance, such as 'RD WK 1 MILE.'
